question.value: How do the size–line width relation, surface density and virial state of molecular gas on 1–100 pc scales compare between the starburst center of NGC253 and the Milky Way Galactic Center?

evidence.quote: We compare molecular gas properties in the starbursting center of NGC253 and the Milky Way Galactic Center (GC) on scales of $\sim1-100$ pc using dendograms and resolution-, area- and noise-matched datasets in CO(1–0) and CO(3–2).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2011.1.00172.S and #2015.1.00274.S.

findings_qualitative.value: Low column density gas in NGC253 (N<3e22) shows constant sigma^2/R, not self-gravitating, likely transient or pressure-bound

evidence.quote: This high-velocity dispersion, not gravitationally self-bound gas is likely in transient structures created by the combination of high average densities and feedback in the starburst.

claims.hypothesis: Do starbursts show increased turbulence at fixed scale?
claims.result: Similar slopes, NGC253 line widths larger by ~2-3
claims.finding: NGC253 has higher velocity dispersion at fixed size

evidence.quote: We find that the size – line width relations in NGC253 and the GC have similar slope, but NGC253 has larger line widths by factors of $\sim2-3$.

claims.experiment: sigma^2/R vs N compared to virial models
claims.result: GC bound above 3e21; NGC253 only above 3e22
claims.finding: Excess line width in NGC253 lies in low-N, unbound gas

evidence.quote: In NGC253 this is only the case for column densities $N>3\times10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$.
